newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis leap, doubt Fed hike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis leap, doubt Fed hike.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds leaped a point, encouraged that an unexpectedly small rise in how much it costs an employer to pay and provide benefits for workers would help keep the central bank from tightening.

Still, even though the Employment Cost Index in the first quarter only rose 0.6 percent--less than 0.9 percent predicted in a Reuters consensus suvery of economists--the market still has to wait and see if the tame wage inflation that report depicted would be confirmed by other reports due this week.
"We'll see what happens, but they certainly took some of the tightening out of the market today," a trader said.
Traders noted there had been speculation that the index would exceed the consensus estimates, which also helped strengthen the market's positive reaction when the actual level confounded such fears.

Institutions appeared confident about buying into the rally, as the New York City Municipal Water Authority said it raised the size of the offering to $701 mllion from $660 million, and extended the final maturity to 2029, two years longer than its traditional 30-year maxium.

Despite the rally, the City of Gulf Breeze, Fla., which became the second municipality to sell inflation-indexed bonds, was forced to raise the spread over the six-months Consumer Price Index to 180 basis points.

The deal, whose lead underwriter was Raymond James, first was pencilled in at around 155 basis points over, which worked out to 30 basis points more than the first such sale by Orlando, Fla. That offering was underwritten by Goldman, Sachs & Co.

Peter Delahunt, national sales manager for Raymond James, said that both the issuer and underwriter were pleased with the way the offering went, even though the size of the sale was fell a bit short of predictions that institutions would order around $100 million of the bonds.
He explained the final spread over the change in the inflation gauge was determined through a Dutch auction. "It was a Dutch auction, so it cleared at $81.5 million, and we're real happy."

The big buyers included nuclear decommissioning funds, long- and intermediate-term funds, insurance companies, and money managers, Delahunt said, explaining he expected retail buyers to be directly involved in future deals.

The rally in fixed-income markets also was aided by another surprisingly weak economic report, durable goods orders for March, which fell 0.3 percent. Economists had expected the report to show orders were flat.

However, intermediate municipal bonds did not fully participate in the gains, as traders said concerns that buyers might have a hard time getting rid of that debt if the market turned down later in the week curbed their rise.
"The intermediate stuff is up an 0.5 percent, roughly half a point, but meeting resistance, because of liquidity (concerns) that if the number is bad on Friday, you need to get out," a trader said.
The Labor Department on Friday is slated to release April payrolls, which economists polled by Reuters forecast would gain 211,000, according to a consensus survey.

But ahead of that important gauge of how successful displaced workers are in finding jobs, the National Association of Purchasing Managment on Wednesday puts out its data that gives traders a look at whether manufacturers are expanding or contracting.

In the secondary market, Chicago Illinios Board of Education Chicago School Reform of December 2020, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.96 percent NET, down eight basis points. In early afternoon trade, they were only off five basis points.

And Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, JFK Internationational Air Terminal LLC Projects of December 2022, which pay a 5.75 percent coupon, were bid at 5.98 percent, NET, down seven basis points. This was off one basis point further than in early afternoon trade.
June municipal bond futures rose 44 ticks to 113-30/32, while June Treasury bonds climbed 49 ticks 108-30/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 160 ticks.
